Mirror

Static mirroring preserves pages, not the Worker services.

The public pages and local WASM self-tests can be served as a static AGPL-3.0 bundle. The canonical site also uses a Cloudflare Worker, Durable Objects, R2, GitHub downloads, and DNS; those dynamic services are not reproduced by copying files.

Why mirror

The architecture expects you to.

Resilience is not a feature we add on top. It is the default state. A network that depends on one website to function is not a network. A network that depends on one website to be discoverable is a different problem, and this page is the answer to it.

Censorship resistance.

State actors block domains. Registrars seize them. CDNs unilaterally deplatform. Hosting providers terminate. Every link in the chain that brings this page to your browser is a single point of failure. Mirroring removes it.

Trust verification.

A mirror can prove bundle equality only when the signed website manifest is fresh and every listed hash matches. The checked-in manifest is currently stale, so that proof is unavailable until the offline signer publishes a new manifest. Even a passing website check would not prove reproducible application releases.

Latency + locality.

A local mirror can reduce document latency and preserve static pages. Its exact compressed size changes, and it does not provide the canonical Worker, Durable Object, R2, GitHub, DNS, presence, or transfer services by itself.

It is yours, in every sense.

AGPL-3.0 permits copying and modification. Static mirrors preserve published pages while reachable; they do not prove that daemon discovery, rendezvous, relays, updates, downloads, or the network continue without their current operators.

One command

The fastest path. Clone, verify, serve, in one step.

An onion service needs no public DNS or public CA, and ordinary clients are not directly given the origin address. Tor, network observers, host configuration, provider logs, or compromise can still expose metadata.

# review the script first (recommended for a privacy-tool mirror)
curl -sSLO https://weareone-link.org/mirror.sh
less mirror.sh
bash mirror.sh

# or, for the impatient
bash <(curl -sSL https://weareone-link.org/mirror.sh)

The script clones the repo into ./one-link-website/, verifies the signed manifest, then starts a local server at http://localhost:8080. Press Ctrl+C to stop. The clone stays around for further hosting (Caddy, nginx, Tor) per the sections below.

Source of the script: /mirror.sh. It verifies the site-manifest signature and all listed hashes, and must fail on the current stale manifest. The website signature does not sign or attest application release artifacts.

Three minutes, by hand

Run a local copy manually.

If you do not want to run a script written by us, the same three steps it does, executed by hand. Python 3 only, no other dependencies.

The static pages and purely local primitive self-tests render from a simple server. API-dependent presence, chat relay, sharing, session registration, topology, and download routing do not work unless the mirror deploys compatible services.

Five minutes

Run a public mirror.

For your community. Behind a domain you own, on a VPS, Raspberry Pi, or home server. Caddy reverse-proxies and gets you a Let's Encrypt cert automatically.

sudo apt install caddy
git clone https://github.com/coherence-energy-labs/one-link-website /var/www/one-link

cat > /etc/caddy/Caddyfile << 'EOF'
your-mirror-domain.example {
    root * /var/www/one-link/dist/weareone-link.org
    file_server
    encode br gzip

    header /css/*    Cache-Control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"
    header /live/*   Cache-Control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"
    header /images/* Cache-Control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"
    header /*.html   Cache-Control "public, max-age=0, must-revalidate"

    header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data: blob:; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; worker-src 'self'; manifest-src 'self'; media-src 'self' blob:; object-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; frame-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; upgrade-insecure-requests"
    header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload"
    header X-Content-Type-Options nosniff
    header Referrer-Policy "no-referrer"
    header Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy "require-corp"
    header Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy "same-origin"
    header Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy "same-origin"
    header Permissions-Policy "interest-cohort=(), browsing-topics=()"
}
EOF

sudo systemctl reload caddy

Caddy gets the cert automatically. Your mirror is online with the same security headers as the canonical site. Point your DNS A/AAAA records at your VPS, wait for the cert, and you are live.

Ten minutes

Onion service on Tor.

An onion service needs no public DNS or public CA, and ordinary clients are not directly given the origin address. Tor, network observers, host configuration, provider logs, or compromise can still expose metadata.

Then run a tiny local server on 127.0.0.1:8080 serving the static bundle (same python3 -m http.server 8080 as above, run as a systemd service so it survives reboots).

Decentralized hosting

IPFS pin.

For content-addressed hosting that does not depend on any single domain or provider. Anyone with the CID can fetch the bundle through any IPFS gateway. The bytes are identical to what we serve.

Content remains available only while at least one reachable node or provider pins it and clients can reach a gateway or IPFS peer. A CID proves content addressing, not perpetual availability.

If you want a stable hostname, point an IPNS record or a DNSLink TXT record at the CID and update it when the content changes. The signed manifest in the bundle is the integrity proof; the CID is the addressing proof.

Verify before you serve

Make sure the bytes are real.

The checked-in /manifest.json has a valid historical signature but stale asset hashes after current changes. Run the verifier: it must report failure. Do not call this website bundle verified until a new offline-signed manifest matches every tracked asset.

cd one-link-website
python3 scripts/verify-manifest.py

# expected output:
#   manifest signature: historical signature validates
#   current verdict:    stale asset hashes; verification must fail

If verification fails, do not host the bundle. Open an issue and pull a fresh clone. The verification script is itself in the repository and itself verifiable.

Tell the world

Your mirror, on the list.

An onion service needs no public DNS or public CA, and ordinary clients are not directly given the origin address. Tor, network observers, host configuration, provider logs, or compromise can still expose metadata.

You are also free to mirror without listing. The point is not centralization of the mirror list, it is the existence of mirrors.
